model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention from CET1 growth

equity_bridge.note: (13.4% - 13.0%) x RWA 369,264 at 2026-07-31, Q3 FY2026 report. Retention path is calibrated to 13.0%, so this surplus is distributable without impairing growth.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR 15.8% vs equity 5yr 9.3% (>30% divergence): the 5yr EPS window starts at the COVID-provision trough (FY2020 EPS 4.11). 3yr figures (rev 10.1 / EPS 8.7 / equity 8.5) agree and are the better guide, and both reflect a favourable rate cycle that the forward path does not extrapolate.
historical_growth.notes: FY2022->FY2025 and FY2020->FY2025, post-split basis. FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for a bank (OCF is dominated by deposit/repo flows) and are left null. Equity includes preferred shares and LRCN-related equity.

scenario_narratives.base: CIBC's earnings settle from a cyclical high rather than keep compounding at the 9-quarter double-digit pace. Revenue grows 7% next year on the current run-rate (Q3 FY26 +15% YoY, NIM stable to gently rising, wealth AUM +19%), fading to 3% as capital-markets and wealth fees normalise and the domestic mortgage book grows low-single-digit. The pre-tax-to-common margin eases from 37.9% to 37.0% as positive operating leverage is offset by loan-loss provisions drifting toward a ~0.40% through-the-cycle ratio. Retention keeps CET1 at ~13%; everything else (~65-75% of earnings) goes out as dividends and buybacks. Terminal at 14x FCFE (~11x earnings), in line with the Canadian-bank long-run range, not today's ~14.5x forward P/E.
scenario_narratives.bull: The U.S. Commercial Banking/Wealth and U.S. Capital Markets build-out keeps delivering (U.S. segment NI nearly doubled in FY25, U.S. capital-markets revenue +39%), the mortgage renewal wall passes with losses contained, and AI-driven efficiency (adjusted efficiency already 52%) takes the margin to ~39.5%. Revenue grows 9% then fades to 3%; ROE holds above the 15% target, and the market keeps paying a 15x FCFE exit multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Canadian mortgage renewal wall (~6% of the book facing 40%+ payment shocks in 2026) meets rising unemployment and U.S. tariffs: impaired loans climb, PCLs roughly double to ~0.70% of loans (~C$4.3bn vs C$2.3bn TTM), and capital-markets/wealth revenue (~a quarter of the total) reverses from a cyclical peak. Revenue growth drops to 1-3%, margin falls to ~30.5% in year two before recovering only to 34%, tax edges to 24%, and the exit multiple de-rates to 12x FCFE. Solvency is not in question (CET1 13.4%, LCR 127%); this is an earnings and multiple reset.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is valued on the cash it can distribute to common shareholders after retaining enough capital to grow its balance sheet at a constant CET1 ratio, discounted at the cost of equity with deposits treated as operating funding (net debt zero). CIBC is a high-quality oligopoly franchise currently earning above its own ROE target on a favourable rate, fee and buyback cycle; the valuation asks what it is worth if that profitability partly normalises rather than extrapolating peak quarters.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit: Canadian mortgage renewal wall and unemployment; every +10bp of loan-loss ratio is ~C$600M pre-tax (~5% of earnings)
Capital-markets and wealth fee normalisation from a cyclical high (Capital Markets ~21% of revenue)
Terminal value carries most of the value; the 14x FCFE cap binds in the base case, so the exit multiple is the single most important assumption
CAD/USD: the NYSE quote converts a CAD valuation at a dated FX rate (0.7019); FX moves the USD value one-for-one
Caribbean sale (close H1 2027) treated as value-neutral; CET1 release at close is unmodelled upside
Automated multiples check mis-scales CM (USD-quoted/CAD-reported): its P/B and P/E bands are not usable for this ticker until it compares like currencies; see sanity_check_response
valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_response: 2026-10-04 sanity trip ('implied P/B 1.43x exceeds 1.5x the 10yr max 0.85x') reviewed; NO driver changed, because the trip is a units artefact on both sides of the comparison, not an over-valuation. (1) The historical band divides a USD NYSE price series that is also adjusted below the actual close (FY2025 'price' 58.17 vs a US$82-86 NYSE close and C$116.21 on the TSX) by CAD book and CAD EPS. That is why it shows CIBC at 0.43-0.85x book and 4.6-6.5x earnings, which it never traded at. (2) The implied 1.43x divides the USD IV (97.13 weighted) by CAD book. On a consistent CAD basis (TSX October close / common equity net of preferreds and other equity instruments / period-end shares): FY2017 ~1.7x, FY2020 ~1.2x, FY2023 ~0.95x (trough), FY2025 ~1.9x, today 2.43x (C$158.27 / C$65.15 = (67,194 - 8,048) / 907.9M at 2026-07-31). FY2020/FY2023 preferred balances are approximate. The model's weighted IV C$138.37 is 2.12x book (base 2.13x, bull 2.52x, bear 1.60x) and ~13.3x TTM adjusted EPS to common (C$10.41), against a FY-end P/E range of ~9.5-13.6x. Both sit inside 1.5x the genuine 10-year maximum and BELOW today's market multiple. Levers rejected: (a) raising CoE above 9.5% would charge the mortgage-renewal, tariff and capital-markets risks twice, since they already sit in the 20%-weighted bear flows (PCL ~0.70%, margin 30.5%, 12x exit); (b) the 'projected growth 8.5%' flag reads historical_growth.selected_growth_rate (the FY22-25 equity CAGR), not the forecast. The base revenue path is 7.0% fading to 3.0% (about 4.5% average), already below the 7.7% through-cycle CAGR; (c) an exit-P/B cap keyed to a 0.85x band would value a 15%-ROE bank at roughly a third of its market price on a mis-scaled history. The defect to fix is the price/currency basis of the multiples check for CAD-filers quoted in USD, not this valuation.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for NYSE CM at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 79.32-124.86 USD; TSX CM.TO and CADUSD=X used for the parity check in inputs.fx_note
data_sources.financials: CM_Metrics.csv / CM.duckdb core_metrics and kpis (FY2015-Q3 FY2026); Q3 FY2026 Report to Shareholders (CM_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt) for adjusted earnings, items of note, pref/LRCN distributions, RWA, CET1, shares and goodwill; FY2025 Annual Report for Q4 FY25 derivation

inputs.share_count_basis: 907.935M common shares outstanding at 2026-07-31 (Q3 FY2026 report, end of period) plus ~7.5M dilutive securities (Q3 weighted-average diluted 919.211M less basic 911.667M). Held FLAT: buybacks (C$3.5bn TTM, new 30M-share NCIB) are funded out of the FCFE the model already pays to shareholders, so shrinking the count as well would double-count them.
inputs.sbc_source: Equity-settled share-based award expense from the Q3 FY2026 statement of changes in equity (C$30M 9M-FY26, ~C$40M TTM). CIBC's main awards (RSAs/PSUs/DSUs) are cash-settled and already expensed inside non-interest expenses, so they sit inside pre-tax earnings and are charged in full; only the equity-settled sliver is added back to 'EBITDA' and re-charged via sbc_pct_path, which keeps the house/street band almost collapsed.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-07-31: Q4 FY25 C$393M + Q1-Q3 FY26 C$1,003M + 890M + 1,199M. Prior 20M-share NCIB completed for C$2.2bn; new 30M-share NCIB (~3.3% of shares) accepted by TSX 2026-06-04. Actual cash, not authorization.
inputs.fx_note: Model in CAD (statements, flows, CoE); quote is the NYSE listing CM in USD. Converted at CADUSD 0.7019 (Yahoo CADUSD=X, close 2026-10-03). Parity check: TSX CM.TO C$158.27 x 0.7019 = US$111.09 vs NYSE CM US$111.02 (0.06% tie) on the 2026-10-02 regular close. One NYSE share = one TSX common share.
inputs.fy0: TTM to Q3 FY2026 (12 months to 2026-07-31)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.5% in CAD: Government of Canada 10y ~3.3% + beta ~1.1 x 5.5% ERP = ~9.4%, rounded to 9.5%. Single rate across scenarios (credit-cycle and capital-markets risk live in the bear flows, not in the discount rate). Sits between NAB.AX 9.7% and the Canadian-bank consensus 9-10%.
inputs.lease_treatment: n/a for a bank FCFE: lease costs (IFRS 16 depreciation + interest) are already inside non-interest expenses and therefore inside pre-tax earnings; no lease liabilities in the bridge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flow is earnings to COMMON: NCI (~C$40M/yr, mostly the 8.3% minority in CIBC Caribbean) and preferred/LRCN distributions (Q3 FY26 run-rate C$128M/qtr = ~C$512M/yr) are removed inside the margin as a pre-tax equivalent (~C$717M at 23%). Preferred shares and LRCNs are therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank FCFE at cost of equity via the component engine (house precedent NAB.AX, TFC, USB, WFC, STT). Deposits are operating funding, so net_debt = 0. Mapping: revenue = NII + non-interest income (TTM 32,348 = Q4 FY25 7,576 + 9M FY26 24,772); 'EBITDA' = ADJUSTED pre-tax income (TTM ~12,923: reported 12,614 + C$297M 9M items of note incl. the C$269M Caribbean-sale charge, + ~C$12M Q4 FY25 intangible amortization) less the pre-tax equivalent of pref/LRCN distributions and NCI (~717) plus equity-settled SBC (~40) = 12,246 = 37.86% of revenue; D&A 0 (software amortization is a real recurring cost already in NIE); 'capex' = capital retention needed to grow CET1 with the balance sheet = (CET1 at 13.0% x RWA 369,264 = 48,004) / revenue = 148.4% x g/(1+g); tax 23% (adjusted effective rate 22.9% 9M FY26). FY0 check: (37.86% - 0.12%) x 32,348 x 0.77 = 9,400 vs adjusted NI to common TTM ~9,526 (9M 7,431 + Q4 FY25 ~2,095) and Q3 run-rate ~10,040. last_fcf 6,385 = TTM adjusted NI to common 9,526 less year-1 retention at 9.71% of revenue (3,141); reported_fcf 6,425 is that before the 40 equity-settled SBC charge -- a bank has no meaningful reported FCF (OCF swings by tens of billions with deposit and repo flows). Excess CET1 above a 13.0% operating level (13.4% actual at 2026-07-31) added in the bridge. CIBC Caribbean sale to Butterfield (~US$1.8bn cash + ~22% Butterfield stake, close H1 2027) treated as roughly value-neutral: it was sold near book (C$269M charge), the lost Caribbean earnings are partly replaced by the equity-accounted Butterfield stake, and the CET1 release at close is NOT added (unquantified upside). Price: NYSE USD quote, model CAD, converted via fx_rate.

base.capex_note: Capital retention = 148.4% (CET1 at 13.0% / revenue) x g/(1+g) for that year's growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): a concentrated Canadian mortgage book at a renewal peak, elevated Canadian unemployment and tariff risk are live, and capital-markets revenue is at a cyclical high. Base 55%: medium-term targets (7-10% EPS growth, 15%+ ROE) are being met or beaten and the base path assumes only partial normalisation. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs U.S. growth, benign credit and continued fee strength to all hold at once, after the stock has already re-rated to ~2.4x book.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality, regulatory single point of failure
Projected growth 8.5% exceeds the through-cycle revenue CAGR 7.7%

sanity_check.fix_applied: No driver changed. Root-caused the trip to a currency-direction defect in scripts/sanity_check.py historical_table() for this ticker: inputs.fx_rate (0.7019, CAD->USD) follows dcf_engine.py's documented convention (currency->quote_currency, used to produce the USD headline IV from the CAD-denominated model -- confirmed against tests/test_dcf_engine.py::TestCurrency and the WISE.L/APA fixtures). sanity_check.py::historical_table applies the SAME stored fx_rate in the OPPOSITE direction (quote_currency->currency, per its own docstring and tests/test_sanity_check.py::test_the_fx_rate_is_quote_to_reporting), to convert the fetched USD NYSE price series into CAD before dividing by CAD book value/EPS. Multiplying a USD price by the CAD->USD rate instead of dividing by it produced FY-end anchor prices roughly half the real NYSE close (e.g. FY2025 58.17 vs an actual ~82-86 close), understating the entire historical P/B and P/E band. This is a latent defect affecting any ticker with currency != quote_currency, not specific to CM -- left unfixed here because it is shared, test-pinned infrastructure (both conventions are asserted by passing tests) that needs a maintainer decision, not a one-ticker patch. Recomputed the comparison by hand on a consistent CAD basis (TSX close / CAD book&EPS) instead: see valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_response for the full walkthrough.

implied_multiples_after_fix.basis: CAD throughout (TSX close, CAD book value and EPS), hand-computed outside the script to bypass the fx-direction defect
implied_multiples_after_fix.conclusion: weighted IV 2.12x CAD book and ~13.3x CAD EPS sit inside 1.5x the real 10yr max and below the current market multiple (2.43x book) -- the model is not implying a valuation the market has never paid
